evidence: Transmat released Carl Craig's debut single, 'Elements,' under the alias Psyche in 1989, while Craig was working as Derrick May's assistant at the label; the early Transmat-era material was later collected on the compilation 'Elements 1989-1990.' Documented in Craig's Wikipedia biography, the Wikipedia article on the compilation, and Transmat's own label record on this map.

trackPair.whatToListenFor: 'Strings of Life' is techno reaching for euphoria in broad daylight. 'Elements,' made two years later inside the same label, is quieter and more interior, described by reissue notes as 'swooning electro-jazz.' Same label, same machine palette, a different temperament entirely.

explanation: Derrick May's label Transmat put out Carl Craig's first record in 1989, while Craig was working there as May's assistant. It sounded like techno, but softer and jazzier than May's own records. Transmat is the line between the first and second waves of Detroit techno: May's decision to take Craig on and put out his early work gave a teenager a working studio and a way to release records before he had any of his own, ahead of Craig founding Planet E in 1991.
